decisions.reason: As a renamed and improved trommel screen based on an already accepted machine, it fits the firm's core screening business and would normally stay in the portfolio.
The mobile flail shredder line is closely aligned with the firm's mobile recycling machinery focus, so management would usually keep developing and selling it rather than withdraw it quickly.
Although less prominently presented, the mobile high-speed grinder serves core waste and biomass processing applications and is still likely to be retained in a long-cycle machinery portfolio.

The stationary electric fine shredder is somewhat more niche, but its electric and resource-efficient positioning matches the firm's strategic direction toward tougher and more sustainable processing solutions.
This green-waste grinder variant is more specialized and therefore carries higher portfolio risk, yet it still addresses important composting and biomass customers the firm serves.
The stationary single-shaft pre-shredder line has strong strategic fit with the firm's established shredding range and would typically be kept as part of a broad industrial processing portfolio.
